g.text: Module Registry -- init() self-registration via blank imports
g.title: Each module calls registry.Register() from its init() function. main.go triggers registration with blank imports: _ "github.com/PranavRJoshi/Veil/modules/syscall" Adding a new module requires no changes to core code.
raw_syscalls/sys_enter tracepoint. Captures every syscall entry: PID, UID, syscall number. Filter maps: pid_filter, uid_filter, syscall_filter (allow + deny each).
kprobes on vfs_open, vfs_read, vfs_write. Captures file path (from dentry), operation type, PID, UID. Filter maps: pid_filter, uid_filter (allow + deny each).

4 hooks: kprobe/tcp_v4_connect, kretprobe/inet_csk_accept, kprobe/inet_listen, tracepoint/sock/inet_sock_set_state. Captures src/dst IP, port, TCP state transitions, PID. Filter maps: pid_filter, uid_filter, port_filter (allow + deny each).

sched/sched_switch tracepoint. Captures context switches: prev/next PID, comm, CPU, scheduling priority, prev state (RUNNING / SLEEPING / ...). Filter maps: pid_filter, uid_filter, cpu_filter (allow + deny each).

kprobe + kretprobe on handle_mm_fault. Captures page fault type (major/minor), faulting address, PID, UID. Filter maps: pid_filter, uid_filter, fault_filter (allow + deny each). Internal: fault_scratch (BPF_MAP_TYPE_PERCPU_ARRAY) correlates kprobe/kretprobe pairs.

g.text: BPF Hash Maps: allow (pid, uid, syscall, port, cpu, fault) | deny (_deny variants)
armed-but-empty map drops all events -- filter_cfg array map (bitmask) tracks which maps are active per module
g.title: BPF_MAP_TYPE_HASH maps store filter keys as u64. Each module has allow and deny variants per filter type. filter_cfg is a BPF_MAP_TYPE_ARRAY holding a bitmask: bit 0 = pid_filter active, bit 1 = uid_filter active, etc. If bitmask is 0, all events pass (no filtering). If a bit is set (armed) but the map has no entries, every event is dropped -- configured-but-unpopulated means drop-all, not pass-all.
Each module uses a BPF ring buffer per module instance. More efficient than perf event arrays: - no per-CPU memory waste - variable-size records - kernel-to-userspace notification via epoll
Uses cilium/ebpf's ringbuf.Reader. Polls the ring buffer fd via epoll and delivers raw event bytes as they arrive. One reader goroutine per active module.

Each module's parseEvent manually decodes raw bytes into a typed Go struct (SyscallEvent, FileEvent, etc.) using binary.LittleEndian.Uint32/Uint64 with explicit field offsets. Not encoding/binary.Read -- fields are extracted by byte position.

After BPF-level filtering, each module applies Go-side predicates for patterns BPF maps cannot express: - scheduler: substring match on comm name - files: file path prefix / operation type Events that do not match are discarded before the sink pipeline.

Optional outer wrapper, present only when --enrich is specified. Adds fields from /proc before passing to PausableSink: - comm: /proc/PID/comm - resolved username from /etc/passwd - timestamp (monotonic or wall clock) Enrichment runs before the pause check -- events during interactive mode are enriched and then dropped by PausableSink.

Always wraps the base sink (TextSink or JSONSink). When the readline prompt is active, Emit() checks an atomic.Bool and drops the event immediately (no blocking, no queue). PausableSink.Pause() / Resume() called by the interactive control loop.
Base sink. Formats each event as key=value pairs on stdout. Default output mode (no flag needed). Format function is module-specific, dispatched via DispatchTextFormat().
Base sink alternative. Marshals each event's field map to a JSON object on its own line (NDJSON format). Enabled with --output json. Mutually exclusive with TextSink.

svg.text: OR (--count-only): CountSink replaces the entire pipeline above

g.text: aggregate by field, print summary on exit
g.title: When --count-only is set, sink is replaced entirely by CountSink. PausableSink and EnrichSink are NOT in the chain. Aggregates event counts keyed by a field (default: comm, overridable with --count-by). Prints a sorted top-N summary to stderr on Close(). CountSink does not stream per-event output.

readline-backed REPL. Activated by SIGINT (Ctrl-C) during tracing. Tab-completion for commands and map names. BEL sound on unrecognised tab input. Commands: add, del, list, clear, status, resume, quit.

Unix domain socket server running concurrently with tracing. Clients send newline-delimited commands and receive responses. Socket chmod 0666 so non-root clients can connect. Same Handler as interactive mode -- no code duplication.

Single Handler shared by both transports. Parses command strings (add/del/list/clear/status) and delegates to MapUpdater. Returns string responses (OK / WARN / ERR). Safe to call from concurrent goroutines.
When only one module is active, buildUpdater() returns the module's own MapUpdater directly. Commands like "add pid 1234" work without a module prefix. No compositeUpdater wrapper is created.

Built only when two or more modules are active. A static mapOwnership table routes each map name to owning modules: "pid" -> all active modules "port" -> network only "syscall" -> syscall only Collects errors from all modules without short-circuiting.

svg.text: updates BPF filter maps at runtime
